return_lantern.name: Lantern of Return
return_lantern.account: A lantern turns above the public well. Its light is repeated in small roof charms and copper-colored marks along the roads. The lantern keepers say it remembers footsteps, especially those made by somebody coming home tired.
return_lantern.custom: Before a neighbor leaves, someone names a place at the supper table for their return. The charmwright repairs roof beads; the inn keeps the return stories.

quiet_measure.name: The Quiet Measure
quiet_measure.account: Two cups hang from a floating beam above the market well. The same pale light marks nearby roofs and roads. Traders call this the Quiet Measure. They argue that a fair exchange includes the work that made an object useful.
quiet_measure.custom: A mender puts a repaired thing on the counter before naming a price. The market keeps a place for exchanges of labor, and neighbors bring troublesome objects to the charmwright.

rootlight_crown.name: The Rootlight Crown
rootlight_crown.account: A small crown of root and leaf floats above the well. Green roof beads repeat its light through the lanes. Gatherers say the crown belongs to the first seed the commons agreed to share, rather than to the person who found it.
rootlight_crown.custom: Households exchange a cutting with a new neighbor. Herb beds and the apothecary face daily needs; the charmwright tends the little lights above their roofs.

traveler_star.name: The Travelers Star
traveler_star.account: A six-point star turns above the well. Its light appears again over roofs and along the town roads. Caravan families say the star was once a lost camp lantern that learned to stay where travelers could find company.
traveler_star.custom: A departing caravan leaves road news with the inn. The next arriving traveler receives a cup before being asked for a name. Letter writers and charmwrights work beside the supply shops.

spore_chorus.name: The Spore Chorus
spore_chorus.account: A cap-shaped charm hangs above the well, surrounded by pale beads of light. Matching pink lights hover over household roofs. The commons calls this the Spore Chorus, though neighbors disagree about whether it has ever sung aloud.
spore_chorus.custom: A new household lends a story to the common supper. Spore gardens, the herbal counter and the charmwright share a lane, so a strange neighbor can still find ordinary help.

borrowed_ember.name: The Borrowed Ember
borrowed_ember.account: An ember hangs above the well and turns slowly without a brazier. Warm-colored roof beads and road marks repeat its light. The town calls it borrowed because every household promises to look after somebody beyond its own hearth.
borrowed_ember.custom: Before a long journey, neighbors ask who will receive the traveler at the other end. The tea shop and winterroot beds serve the hearth lanes, and the charmwright keeps the roof lights in repair.
